label: seizei
title_raw: せいぜい (精精) ([せいぜい] )(seizei)
title: せいぜい (精精)
meaning: my utmost,  at most できるだけ。精一杯。最大限。

examples.japanese: 今度は徹夜になりそうだ。今のうちにせいぜい休んでおこう。
examples.body_text:
今度は徹夜になりそうだ。今のうちにせいぜい休んでおこう。 

		It looks like overtime work ahead. For now I will 
		do my utmost 
		to relax.
examples.body_html:
今度は徹夜になりそうだ。今のうちにせいぜい休んでおこう。 
It looks like overtime work ahead. For now I will do my utmost to relax.

examples.japanese: この仕事だったらせいぜい三日もあればできる。
examples.body_text:
この仕事だったらせいぜい三日もあればできる。 

		If it's this type of work, it can be done in about three days 
		at the outside.
examples.body_html:
この仕事だったらせいぜい三日もあればできる。 
If it's this type of work, it can be done in about three days at the outside.

examples.japanese: この仕事の完成にせいぜい努力します。
examples.body_text:
この仕事の完成にせいぜい努力します。 

		I will exert 
		my best 
		in finishing this work.
examples.body_html:

I will exert my best in finishing this work.

examples.japanese: あの婦人はせいぜい40歳だ。
examples.body_text:
あの婦人はせいぜい40歳だ。 

		The lady is forty years old

あの婦人はせいぜい40歳だ。

		ten minutes' walk from here.
examples.body_html:

It is no more than ten minutes' walk from here.

examples.body_text:
この辞書はせいぜい２万語くらいしか載っていない。 

		This dictionary contains 
		not more than 
		20,000 words.
examples.body_html:

Not more than

comments.text: Note that せいぜい also has the meaning of "at th emost." For example, せいぜい３日もあればできる would mean "It can be done in about three days at the very outside," In this sense it has the meaning similar to たかだか.

comments.text:
'At the very outside' means "at the worst". maybe literally, "on the border of what might and might not happen" 

-> さいていの場合、三日掛かる。

comments.text: hmm it would be 最長（さいちょう）instead of 最低（さいてい）. 最長⇔最短（さいたん）、最高（さいこう）⇔最低

comments.text: You guys must mean 最悪の場合. You would not say さいていの場合、三日掛かる but could say さいてい三日掛かる, which would mean "takes the minimum of three days."The former says that it could be done in less than three days, but the latter would say it takes three days or more.

comments.text: I guess "at the very outside" is awkward, but I think "at the outside" should be acceptable.

comments.text: While I can't comment on any of the Japanese - "at the outside" is very informal in English. It refers to the expression "an outside chance" (a term from horseracing). So the first example would be better written: "If it's this type of work, there is an outside chance that it can be done in about three days."
comments.html: While I can't comment on any of the Japanese - "at the outside" is very informal in English. It refers to the expression "an outside chance" (a term from horseracing). So the first example would be better written: "If it's this type of work, there is an outside chance that it can be done in about three days."

comments.text: I have been told by a native speaker that "せいぜい" has a certain ironic or sarcastic tinge to it. It is used in the context of saying that someone "did their best", etc. in an ironic way, meaning it could have been done a bit better.
